decisionsTitle: The newsletter's subscribers as a list, and its letter in rich text
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-09-28 22:48:** «în newsletter vreau să și văd abonații și mailurile lor». **And at 22:52:** «trebuie să pot scrie cu Rich text editor abonaților!». Amends §445, which showed the subscribers as numbers only and took the letter as plain text.

**Decision — the list.** `/admin/newsletter` gains a card «Abonați» / "Subscribers" (`modules/newsletter/ui/NewsletterSubscribers.tsx`): a fold with the `contacts` glyph, closed by default (§336), whose closed line says the counts — «12 abonați confirmați, 3 în așteptare» (`countForm`, no ICU plural). Inside, every subscriber newest first: the address as typed (`delivery_email`), the language, the topics in the pop-up's words, the state, subscribed since and confirmed on (the one date helper, with the weekday, §349), a visible separator under each row (§453), a table from `md` and one block per row below it — the same elements under different CSS, each cell's column name drawn before it from `data-label`, so a row renders its «Dezabonează» form once rather than once per layout (at the 500-row cap, 500 client islands, not 1 000). The former first card, which kept the numbers, the history and the typed-address withdrawal, is renamed «Cifre și trimiteri» / "Numbers and sends" so two cards are not both «Abonați».

- **The state says what the confirmation link is doing** (`domain/subscriber-list.ts#confirmLinkState`), read from `newsletter_tokens` and the outbox with no new column: «Confirmat»; or «În așteptare» with «Linkul de confirmare merge până …», «Emailul de confirmare n-a plecat încă» (the link is minted when the email leaves, §14.5, and since §513 an email waits for the tick) or «Linkul a expirat».
- **Search and filters without JavaScript, the state in the address** (§527's shape): `q`, `topic`, `state`, a GET form whose action carries the card's fragment, the fold opening by itself while a filter is in use. A whole address is canonicalized (§74, AGENTS.md §10.4) and matched on `canonical_email` — `Ana.Pop+club@GoogleMail.com` is found by `ana.pop@gmail.com` — never compared as typed; Gmail's dots stay two identities (version 2). Every search is also a case-blind contains over the address as typed and its canonical form, `%` and `_` escaped — a fragment (`ana`, `@yahoo`) is no address to canonicalize, and a well-formed part of a longer address (`pop@gmail.co`) is still a part, so a whole address finds its identity or any row it is part of: a way to find a row, never an identity decision. A topic is who receives it (its own subscribers and «Toate noutățile»'s, the `receives` rule); «Toate noutățile» itself is who asked for everything; the retired DISCOUNTS is no filter (§517). The counts follow the filter, state included. The table draws at most 500 rows; the counts and the CSV are always the whole filter. A row's link state is read only for a pending row (the two subqueries sit in a CASE on the row's own confirmation), and the CSV, which has no link-state column, reads the subscribers table alone (`exportNewsletterSubscribers`).
- **«Descarcă CSV»** (`GET /api/admin/newsletter/subscribers`, `subscribers-csv.ts`): the table's columns in the reader's language, UTF-8 with a BOM (Excel on Windows reads a CSV without one in the old code page), every cell through the registrations export's `csvCell` (formula characters neutralized, quotes doubled, CRLF), dates ISO 8601, named `newsletter-abonati-<club date>.csv`. The route asserts the page's own role (`canSendNewsletter`) and records `newsletter.subscribers_exported` — who, the filter's shape and the row count, never an address — as the registrations export does (§322), because a downloaded file is the one copy an unsubscribe cannot reach; the guide says to delete it after use.
- **«Dezabonează» on a row**, Administrator and Superadministrator only (`canManageRegistrations`, the threshold of §445's typed-address withdrawal): asked first in the one ConfirmDialog naming the address (§384), done by `unsubscribeNewsletterSubscriber` through the very `deleteSubscriberIn` the subscriber's own «unsubscribe from everything» uses — the row, every link of theirs by cascade, every newsletter still waiting for them — in one transaction with the audit row `newsletter.subscriber_unsubscribed`: the actor, why (`reason: staff_unsubscribe`, `source: subscribers_list`), whether it had confirmed, and the subscriber's id, which names no row afterwards; never the address (the §67/§88 pattern). The toast says it went, or that the address was already gone. An Organizer reads the list and the CSV and is offered no button; the action and the service refuse one on the server (BR-REQ-060-01). A volunteer, the Redactor, Tehnic and a member keep the page's 404.
- **Privacy.** The notice template's newsletter paragraph said what is kept and for how long, not who at the club reads it. One sentence is added to it, both languages: only the club's organizers and administrators see the list with the addresses, in the site's administration area, from which they can download it. The notice in force says none of it until the club approves a new version from the template (`/admin/legal` shows the moved template). No address appears on any page outside the backoffice.
- **The guide** (§441): the Administrator's numbered steps for reading, searching, downloading and unsubscribing, and the Organizer's for reading, with the exact button words; the Organizer's «Scrie abonaților» steps no longer say that addresses do not appear.

**Decision — the letter in rich text.** The composer's two plain boxes become the platform's own editor (`RichTextEditor`), one per language under Română | English tabs (`LocaleTabPanels`), with «Tradu cardul: RO → EN» at the end of the tab row (§514; `newsletterBodyEn` joins the translation allowlist as a rich text). The vocabulary is the email's (§270: paragraphs, two heading levels, lists, a quote, bold, italic, links) **plus pictures the club stored** (`NEWSLETTER_BODY_BLOCKS`): §270 refused pictures in the club's message texts, but a newsletter is a letter the reader asked for, from an address they confirmed, and the owner asked for it with pictures. Every picture must be one this club stored — its address on the local `/api/media/…` route or under the store's public address (`R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`), `newsletterPicturesAreOwn`: the rich-text schema checks only the key's shape (`<uuid>/web.webp`) and would take it on any https host, and a letter reaches every subscriber, so a crafted post could otherwise put a third party's tracking picture in their inboxes; such a body is refused like one the editor does not offer. A film and a table stay refused (no film plays in an inbox; a table breaks a phone), and the editor offers neither (`features.video: false`, a new switch that hides only the film button). A picture is rendered as a centred block at the editor's share of the card's width, its `alt` standing in when the client blocks it; the whole photograph is sent whatever crop or side the page would draw, because a mail client crops and floats nothing reliably; its address is the smallest rung of its ladder at least twice the card's width (§414) and always absolute — `APP_BASE_URL` before the local `/api/media/…` route, the store's public address as stored — so no hostname is written in `src/`. The plain-text half names each picture by its alt and address. Rendered by `newsletterBodyParts` beside `emailBodyParts` in `email-rich-text.ts`, through the one template, so the preview (`NewsletterPreview`, both languages) shows the card the subscriber receives. A picture in a sent newsletter counts as used for the orphan sweep and the pictures page («Într-un newsletter trimis»): the inboxes keep loading it.

- **Storage, no migration.** `newsletter_sends.body` stays `jsonb` `{ ro, en }`; each value is now the editor's document. A send stored before holds plain strings and renders exactly as it did (`readNewsletterWords` reads either); a plain string posted without the editor is read as a document, a blank line a paragraph. The column's shape does not change, so no migration (the journal stays at 0107).
- **The ceiling is counted on the words** (`richTextToPlainText`, 6 000 characters, pictures not counted), said in plain words under the tabs; the posted JSON has its own generous bound. A field in braces is still refused by name. The sends' history shows each letter's first line of words. The new-event alert is untouched.

**The owner, 2026-09-28 23:10:** «oamenii pot să se și dezaboneze de la newsletter». A subscriber could leave only from the link in a message (§445's MANAGE link → «Dezabonează-mă de la tot»); somebody without a message at hand — deleted, on another device — had no door on the site.

**Decision — «Vreau să mă dezabonez» / "I want to unsubscribe".** Under the contact page's newsletter button, a quiet text link with the `unsubscribe` glyph, a native fold (`<details>`, so it opens without a script, 44 px tall) holding a one-box form: the address and «Trimite-mi linkul» / "Send me the link" with the same glyph. Its answer is one sentence whatever the address is — «Dacă adresa e abonată, ai primit un email cu linkul de gestionare.» / "If the address is subscribed, you have received an email with the link to manage it." — so the form says nothing about who reads the club's news (§39, the resend-oracle rule, BR-REQ-031-01 criterion 3). It takes the sign-up's defences unchanged: the honeypot and the timing check answered with the same silence, Turnstile at the action (`requestNewsletterManageLinkAction`), and the sign-up's own per-address bucket (`newsletter-subscribe`, three an hour) — spent before the list is read, so «limited» reveals nothing either, and the two forms together still put at most three messages an hour into one mailbox. A malformed address, a failed check or the spent hour come back with the fold open and the address in the sealed draft (§142), never in the URL (`?nleave=`).

- **Only a confirmed subscriber is written to**, found through the canonical address (AGENTS.md §10.4), in its own language and at its own spelling — never the form's, since whoever typed it may not own it. A pending address has no page yet (its confirmation link is its only link, and the retention sweep deletes it when that expires) and receives no newsletter meanwhile, so it is sent nothing; an unknown address likewise.
- **No new message type, no migration.** The message is `NEWSLETTER_CONFIRM` to an address already subscribed — the one whose render already mints the MANAGE link at send time (§14.5) — with `payload.request = "manage"`, so its words say what was asked: «Cineva — probabil tu — a cerut, pe pagina noastră de contact, linkul abonamentului la noutăți pentru această adresă. Cu butonul de mai jos te dezabonezi de la tot sau îți schimbi temele. Dacă nu ai cerut tu, ignoră emailul: abonamentul rămâne cum e.» (and the English twin). Nothing is changed by the request: the unsubscribe stays the page's POST, by the link, single use (AGENTS.md §12.8) — the mailbox's owner does it, not whoever typed the address.
- **Refused:** unsubscribing straight from the typed address (anyone could remove anyone); a bucket of its own (it would double what one mailbox can be sent in an hour); a message to a pending address (it has nothing to manage yet).

**Refused.** Paging the list (a club newsletter is hundreds of addresses; 500 rows and the whole CSV cover it). A typed reason in the unsubscribe dialog (the one dialog has no text field; the audit row names the list as the reason, and the typed-address form keeps covering a written request). A column or a migration for the link's state (the tokens and the outbox already say it). Keeping the crop and the float in the email (no client draws them the same way).
changelogLine: - **The newsletter's subscribers, a letter in rich text, and a way out from the site** — «Newsletter» → «Abonați» lists every address with its language, topics and state (how long its confirmation link still works), searched through the canonical address and filtered by topic and state in the address bar, and downloads as a CSV; an Administrator unsubscribes a row after a question naming the address; the composer writes each language in the rich-text editor, pictures included, with «Tradu cardul: RO → EN»; and under the contact page's newsletter button «Vreau să mă dezabonez» mails a subscriber the link to their own page, answering the same sentence for any address. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given subscribers on /admin/newsletter, when the «Abonați» card is opened, then every subscriber is listed newest first with the address as typed, the language, the topics, the state — for a pending address how long its confirmation link works, «Emailul de confirmare n-a plecat încă» while the confirmation is queued, or «Linkul a expirat» — the subscription day and the confirmation day, and the closed card's line counts the confirmed and the pending under the filter; a whole address searched is matched on its canonical form (a +tag, capitals and googlemail find the row, another dotting does not) or as part of a longer one (`pop@gmail.co` finds `ana.pop@gmail.com`), a topic filter shows who receives it and a state filter narrows the counts, all in the address (2026-09-28, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a letter written in the newsletter composer's rich-text editor, when it is sent, then `newsletter_sends.body` stores each language's document and the message carries its bold, links, lists and pictures in the HTML and the plain text, every picture's address absolute from APP_BASE_URL, a picture on any host but the club's store refused (the stored key's shape on another host included), a film or a table refused by name and the 6 000-character ceiling counted on the words; a send stored before as plain text still renders, and a picture in a sent newsletter is never taken by the orphan sweep (2026-09-28, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the newsletter's subscribers, when the list, its CSV or «Dezabonează» is asked for, then the Organizer, the Administrator and the Superadministrator read the list and download the CSV (UTF-8 with a BOM, the table's columns, the registrations export's escaping, an audit row without an address), a volunteer is refused the CSV, and only an Administrator or a Superadministrator unsubscribes a row — as the subscriber's own unsubscribe does, the row, its links and its waiting mail deleted, with an audit row naming who and why and never the address — while the service refuses anybody below (2026-09-28, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the contact page's newsletter box, when somebody opens «Vreau să mă dezabonez» / "I want to unsubscribe" and sends an address, then the page answers «Dacă adresa e abonată, ai primit un email cu linkul de gestionare.» whatever the address — subscribed, pending or unknown — behind the sign-up's honeypot, timing check and Turnstile; only a confirmed subscriber, found through the canonical address, is queued one `NEWSLETTER_CONFIRM` marked `request: manage`, to its own address and language, whose link — minted at send time — opens the subscriber's own page, where «Dezabonează-mă de la tot» removes the subscription; a pending or unknown address is queued nothing, and the fourth press in an hour for one address is refused, the bucket shared with the sign-up (2026-09-29, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the newsletter's subscribers as a list with search, a CSV and an unsubscribe, the letter in rich text, and «Vreau să mă dezabonez» on the contact page
